page: Amazon Web Services c8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 96 dedicated physical cores built on the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per physical core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core tests placing in the top 10% of evaluated systems. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth, which supports high-throughput database operations and rapid multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. In specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations, while text generation for medium and large language models ranks as strong.

The bare-metal architecture offers high resource density and eliminates hypervisor overhead, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for highly parallelized workloads. The primary hardware tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage and GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for local-disk-heavy tasks or massive parallel graphics processing. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and medium-to-large LLM text generation.
